name: Uptown Yolk
tagline: Breakfast and brunch from chefs Greg and Subrina Collier in South End.
description: Uptown Yolk serves breakfast and brunch plates from the team behind several Charlotte restaurants. Chef Greg Collier and Subrina Collier run the South End location on South Tryon Street.

_verified.note: QCity 2026 coverage of the Colliers notes Yolk still operating; Toast ordering page live.

name: Mert's Heart and Soul
tagline: Uptown soul food with Lowcountry and Gullah roots since 1998.
description: Mert's Heart and Soul has served soul food in Uptown Charlotte since 1998, with dishes drawn from Lowcountry and Gullah cooking. James and Renee' Bazzelle own the College Street restaurant.

_verified.note: Listed in QCity's oldest Black-owned businesses roundup; WSOC Black-owned spotlight; site live.

name: Sol' Delish
tagline: Soul food plates, wings and yellow rice in University City.
description: Sol' Delish serves soul food in University City, with wings, macaroni and cheese and yellow rice among the regular plates. QCity included it in its 2026 list of Black-owned soul food restaurants.

_verified.note: QCity June 2026 Black-owned soul food list.

name: Mr. Charles Chicken and Fish
tagline: Fried chicken and fish from a Charlotte favorite with more than one location.
description: Mr. Charles Chicken and Fish serves fried chicken, fish and sides from its Statesville Avenue home and other Charlotte locations. QCity counts it among the city's Black-owned soul food spots.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity 2026 soul food list. Multiple locations, so slug carries -charlotte. Zip not confirmed.

name: Freshwaters Southern and New Orleans
tagline: Southern and New Orleans cooking with live music near Uptown.
description: Freshwaters serves Southern and New Orleans dishes on North Graham Street, often with live music. Clifton and Sharon Freshwater own the restaurant.

_verified.note: QCity 2026 Black-owned soul food list. Founded year left null because the site and QCity give different years.

name: Kristy's Creole Kitchen
tagline: Creole cooking from Baton Rouge family recipes in South End.
description: Kristy's Creole Kitchen brings Baton Rouge family recipes to South Boulevard, with gumbo, po'boys and other Creole plates. Owner Kristy Jamison opened the South End spot after building a following for her cooking.

_verified.note: Black-owned per its inclusion in QCity's 2026 Black-owned soul food list; opening covered by QCity.

name: Cuzzo's Cuisine
tagline: Soul food and lobster mac from two cousins in University City.
description: Cuzzo's Cuisine serves soul food plates, including its well known lobster macaroni and cheese, on North Tryon Street. Cousins Andarrio Johnson and Anglee Ellis run the restaurant.

_verified.note: QCity reported its outlet-mall location closing; the University City restaurant remains open and is on the 2026 soul food list.

name: Hilltop Coffee
tagline: Neighborhood coffee shop on Mallard Creek Road.
description: Hilltop Coffee is a neighborhood coffee shop in north Charlotte serving espresso drinks and pastries. Joy Shiver and Rashad Hart own the shop.

_verified.note: In QCity's Black-owned coffee shops roundup. Slug avoids existing hilltop-coffee-kitchen. Zip not confirmed.

name: Gotcha Matcha
tagline: Matcha drinks and lattes from two Uptown shops.
description: Gotcha Matcha serves matcha lattes and other tea drinks in Uptown Charlotte. Owner Eric Hicklen Jr. opened a second Uptown location on South Tryon Street.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity coffee roundup. Two locations; address is the South Tryon shop. No reliable website found.

name: Sugar and Sip Coffee and Workshop
tagline: Coffee shop and coworking space in Uptown's Fourth Ward area.
description: Sugar and Sip pairs a coffee bar with a coworking space on West Fifth Street. Owner Shai Wallace rolls out seasonal drink menus.

_verified.note: QCity covered its summer menu as a Black-owned coffee shop. Top-up 2026-10-15: wrote Fifth as 5th so the address geocodes.

name: The Pauline Tea Bar Apothecary
tagline: Loose leaf tea bar and apothecary in west Charlotte.
description: The Pauline Tea Bar Apothecary serves loose leaf teas and herbal blends from its shop on Arty Avenue. Owner Sherry Waters opened it in 2019 and marked seven years with a month of events.

_verified.note: QCity 2026 seven-year anniversary coverage.

name: Sub One Hoagie
tagline: Hoagies and cheesesteaks on North Graham Street since 1992.
description: Sub One Hoagie has made hoagies and cheesesteaks in Charlotte since 1992. Derek Jones runs the shop near Uptown.

_verified.note: Featured in QCity sponsored roundup of Black-owned Uptown businesses.

name: Eggroll Company
tagline: Stuffed egg rolls with creative fillings at Camp North End.
description: Eggroll Company serves egg rolls stuffed with a rotating set of fillings at Camp North End. Daphne Alexander owns the business.

_verified.note: In QCity's Black businesses of Camp North End roundup. Top-up 2026-10-15: address and phone from own site (c) 2025.

name: Lottie's Cafe
tagline: Cafe and coffee counter inside Uptown's Queen City Quarter.
description: Lottie's Cafe serves coffee, breakfast and light bites inside Queen City Quarter on East Trade Street. Ashley Hines opened the cafe in 2024.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity; also in the 2026 coffee roundup.

name: Big Papa's Empanadas
tagline: Oversized hip hop themed empanadas, late nights in the Historic West End.
description: Big Papa's Empanadas serves oversized empanadas with hip hop themed names from a counter on Rozzelles Ferry Road. Chef Jonathan Leonard opened it in September 2026 with late hours Thursday through Saturday.

_verified.note: QCity Sept 6 2026 calls it Chef Jonathan Leonard's Black-owned counter; soft opened Sept 3 2026.

name: Archive CLT
tagline: Cultural hub and cafe on Beatties Ford Road.
description: Archive CLT is a cultural hub and cafe on Beatties Ford Road that hosts events and preserves Black history alongside its coffee menu. Cheryse Terry opened it in 2022.

_verified.note: Site describes itself as a cultural hub first and cafe second; Black woman-owned per QCity.

name: Harvey B. Gantt Center for African-American Arts + Culture
tagline: Museum of African American art, history and culture in Uptown.
description: The Harvey B. Gantt Center presents exhibitions, programs and performances celebrating African American art and culture. The institution dates to 1974 and sits on South Tryon Street in Uptown.

_verified.note: Black-led nonprofit cultural institution rather than a privately owned business; current exhibits covered by QCity in 2026.

name: DUPP and SWAT
tagline: Creative studio, shop and event space at Camp North End.
description: DUPP and SWAT is a creative studio, retail shop and event space at Camp North End. Siblings Dion and Davita Galloway run it as a home for art, design and community events.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity Camp North End coverage. Top-up 2026-10-15: studio address and phone from own locations page.

name: ASÉ Wrestling
tagline: Independent pro wrestling shows built around Black talent.
description: ASÉ Wrestling stages independent pro wrestling shows in Charlotte with a lineup centered on Black wrestlers. Founder Darius Lockhart launched the promotion in September 2023 and it has run more than a dozen shows.

_verified.note: Black ownership inferred from QCity profile of Black founder and owner Darius Lockhart, not an explicit Black-owned label. Latest show listed Aug 1 2026.

name: How Sanguine
tagline: Dining events and private dinners from Camp North End.
description: How Sanguine hosts ticketed dining events and private dinners from its space at Camp North End. Chann and Montrel Little run the concept.

_verified.note: Unit 120 at Camp North End; Black-owned per QCity. Top-up 2026-10-15: address from own site (c) 2025.

name: Deep Roots CPS Farm
tagline: West Charlotte farm with a seasonal stand and Uptown market sales.
description: Deep Roots CPS Farm grows produce on Primm Road and sells it at an on-site farm stand from June to October and at the Uptown Farmers Market on Saturdays. Cherie and Wisdom Jzar started the farm in 2019.

_verified.note: Slug avoids existing deep-roots-farm. Black-owned per Black Farmers Index and Blavity.

name: Russell Brothers Farms
tagline: Family farm and farm store in Midland, east of Charlotte.
description: Russell Brothers Farms raises and sells farm products from its farm store on Drake Road in Midland. The store is open Tuesday through Sunday.

_verified.note: Black-owned proof is directory only (Black Farmers Index).

name: Watkins Grove Farm
tagline: CSA produce boxes from a North Carolina Black-owned farm.
description: Watkins Grove Farm offers CSA produce boxes to customers in the Charlotte area. Sign-ups run through the farm's website.

_verified.note: Black-owned proof is directory only. Draft because recent activity and exact farm location could not be confirmed.

name: Humble Holistic Farm
tagline: Small farm and Sunday country store in Kannapolis.
description: Humble Holistic Farm grows produce and runs a country store on Sundays from 12 to 4 on Camp Julia Road in Kannapolis. The farm is listed in the Black Farmers Index.

_verified.note: Black-owned proof is directory only. Draft because the site shows no updates dated 2024 to 2026.

name: Shelves Bookstore
tagline: Charlotte bookstore selling online and through book subscriptions.
description: Shelves Bookstore sells books online and through a monthly book subscription after starting as a Charlotte pop-up. Owner Abbigail Glen founded it in 2019.

_verified.note: Listed in Book Riot's 2026 Black-owned bookstores list.

name: SpringClean
tagline: Nonprofit sustainable clothing boutique at Camp North End.
description: SpringClean is a nonprofit boutique selling secondhand and sustainable clothing at Camp North End. CT Anderson founded it in 2019; the shop is open Wednesday through Saturday.

_verified.note: QCity calls it a Black-owned nonprofit boutique.

name: Glowgirl
tagline: Permanent jewelry studio and cafe in South End.
description: Glowgirl is a jewelry studio and cafe on West Boulevard where guests can shop and make pieces. Jorgie McClendon opened it as a community gathering spot, open Thursday through Sunday.

_verified.note: QCity profile is sponsored content; second source is a Sep 2026 event listing that gives the Glowgirl address. No website confirmed.

name: Lip Print Beauty Bar
tagline: Custom lip color studio in Uptown, by appointment.
description: Lip Print Beauty Bar lets guests blend custom lipstick and gloss shades at its Uptown studio. Latrice Reynolds and Nickell Parks own the business and take bookings by appointment.

_verified.note: Featured in QCity sponsored roundup of Black-owned Uptown businesses.

name: Note and Accord
tagline: Perfumery for custom and signature scents in Fourth Ward.
description: Note and Accord is a perfumery offering signature fragrances and custom scent experiences. Nia McAdoo founded it in 2024 and announced a second location.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity. Two locations, so slug carries -charlotte.

name: Cell Therapy
tagline: Salon and barbershop inside Kinship at Camp North End.
description: Cell Therapy is a salon and barbershop inside the Kinship space at Camp North End. It comes from the Galloway siblings behind DUPP and SWAT.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity. No dedicated website confirmed. Top-up 2026-10-15: address and phone from the Dupp & Swat locations page.

name: Wholistic Rebirth
tagline: Massage and bodywork studio inside Kinship at Camp North End.
description: Wholistic Rebirth offers massage and bodywork sessions from the Kinship space at Camp North End. Appointments book through its website.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity Camp North End roundup. Top-up 2026-10-15: address from own site (c) 2026; zip matches How Sanguine on the same street.

name: You vs Yourself (YVY)
tagline: Fitness and performance training center at Camp North End.
description: You vs Yourself runs a 3,000 square foot fitness and performance center at Camp North End. It offers group classes and personal training.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity Camp North End roundup. Top-up 2026-10-15: main location from own site.

name: M&F Bank
tagline: Black-owned community bank with a branch on Beatties Ford Road.
description: M&F Bank is a Black-owned community bank founded in Durham in 1907, with a Charlotte branch on Beatties Ford Road. The branch is open weekdays from 9 to 5.

_verified.note: Minority depository institution. QCity July 2026: merger with Optus Bank announced, expected to close Q4 2026; name and branding may change.

name: Stroud's Flowers
tagline: Family florist on Beatties Ford Road for about 50 years.
description: Stroud's Flowers has arranged flowers for weddings, funerals and everyday occasions on Beatties Ford Road for about 50 years. Christina Nivens now runs the family business.

_verified.note: In QCity oldest Black-owned businesses roundup. Founded year left null because sources say about 50 years.

name: Saint and Society
tagline: Jewelry shop and community space in NoDa.
description: Saint and Society sells jewelry and hosts community events from its shop on East 36th Street in NoDa. Naomi Calvin and Vee Jones opened the storefront in April 2026.

_verified.note: Black- and Latina-owned per QCity.

name: The Finance Bar
tagline: Mobile financial education bus parked at Camp North End.
description: The Finance Bar is a mobile bus offering financial education and money coaching, based at Camp North End's Boileryard. Marsha Barnes opened it in March 2025.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity. No website confirmed.

name: Loyd Visuals
tagline: Photo and video studio run by three brothers at Camp North End.
description: Loyd Visuals is a photo and video production studio run by three brothers. It opened in Camp North End's Mount District in July 2024.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity Camp North End roundup. Top-up 2026-10-15: address from own site.

name: Ms. Elsie's Caribbean Bed and Breakfast
tagline: Caribbean themed bed and breakfast in east Charlotte.
description: Ms. Elsie's Caribbean Bed and Breakfast offers guest rooms with Caribbean touches on North Sharon Amity Road. Owner Cheryl Watkins has operated it for more than two decades.

_verified.note: Black-owned per QCity 2026 B&B list.
